title: A 'please pay' request for a member without the app reaches nobody, and the desk is never told
what: When the desk asks a member to pay, the server turns the request into a phone note only for members linked to the MettleUp app. For anyone else it quietly makes no note. The number of notes made is only written to a log line a minute later; nothing goes back to the desk. On Crispy Curves no roster member is linked to the app (0 of 2), so every 'please pay' request there reaches nobody.
expected: The desk sees, for each request, whether it reached the member's phone, and is offered WhatsApp when it cannot.
how_often: every request for a member without the app
fix_line: Keep how many phones each request reached and show it to the desk, with a WhatsApp button when it is none

title: If the team's reply pop-up fails to send, the member never gets one
what: When the MettleUp team replies to a help question, the phone's pop-up address is wiped as the reply is saved, before the pop-up is tried. If the pop-up then fails (Google busy, our key missing or refused), no address is left, so no later try is possible. The member learns of the reply only when they next open the app.
expected: The address is kept until the pop-up is really handed over, and a failed send is tried again.
fix_line: Clear the address only after the pop-up was handed over

title: A gym with many staff browsers can lose the daily summary on some of them
what: Each minute the staff alert sender may make about 12 outside calls, and urgent alerts spend theirs first. A gym's daily or weekly summary is claimed once, for only as many browsers as the calls left allow; the browsers over that number never get that summary, and it is not sent again.
expected: Every staff browser of the gym gets the summary, even if it takes another minute.
who: owners and staff of gyms with several browsers
how_often: on busy minutes, for gyms with many browsers
fix_line: Send the rest of a claimed summary in the next minute's run
